# Is the Free plan really free?

Details on the Free plan

Written by Canny

June 5, 2026

The Canny Free plan is honestly free. There is no time limit on how long you can be on the Free plan and the included features of the Free plan work the same way they do on paid plans.

Here are a few things to keep in mind if you’re on the Free plan:

brief.interpretation: I interpret this as a one-email acquisition introduction for a product manager or product team lead at a software company. Because the relationship is unknown, the email should introduce one concrete workflow without assuming the recipient uses Gong, Intercom, Slack, or any other named tool. The first ask is to inspect the documented Autopilot mechanism and plan availability before registering.
brief.reader:
Selected audience: Product manager or product team lead at a software company.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (inferred; check applicability): People responsible for product decisions at software companies pull customer feedback from multiple channels (sales/CS calls recorded in tools like Gong, support tickets, Slack) into a central place such as a feedback portal or ProductBoard so requests can be reviewed by the product team rather than lost across departments.
brief.reader_segment: Product manager or product team lead at a software company
brief.promise: Canny can turn feedback embedded in customer conversations into deduplicated requests that are easier for a product team to review and route.
brief.orientation: Canny is customer feedback management and product roadmapping software that pulls feedback out of channels like Gong, Intercom and Slack into one place and merges duplicate requests.
brief.arc: In one email, move the reader from recognizing the limits of handing product teams raw conversation links to understanding how Autopilot extracts and organizes the feedback, then invite them to inspect the documented mechanism and plan availability.
brief.sequence_rationale: One email cannot responsibly cover capture, prioritization, roadmapping, integrations, proof, and pricing. The strongest supported introduction is the operational consequence closest to the audience's verified problem: Autopilot reads conversations, pulls out feature requests, merges duplicates, and triages feedback. A public pricing page is the lowest-friction verified destination because it documents the mechanism and its availability without requiring an account. No alternative argument is included because the other supported propositions either depend on a narrower workflow, rely on a single customer's outcome, or lack an equally well-supported first-step payoff. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign: Can this source be supplied in a readable form or its missing details verified?

emails.selection_reason: This directly addresses the audience's documented need for usable feature requests rather than entire-call links, using the strongest evidence assigned to that problem. It gives a new buyer a concrete reason to consider Canny without assuming a particular installed tool.

value_case.reader_benefit: If customer feedback reaches the team through calls, support conversations, or reviews, Canny can give the product team extracted, deduplicated feedback to review instead of leaving each request buried in its source conversation.
value_case.mechanism: Autopilot reads call transcripts, support tickets, and reviews, pulls out feature requests, merges detected duplicates, and triages feedback to the appropriate team.
decision_conditions: Autopilot is included in all plans.

emails.target_audience: Product manager or product team lead at a software company
emails.job: Get the reader to inspect how Autopilot converts customer conversations into deduplicated, triaged feedback and decide whether that workflow merits a free evaluation.
emails.single_idea: Canny Autopilot can pull feature requests out of customer calls, tickets, and reviews, merge duplicates, and triage the resulting feedback so a product team can work from requests rather than raw conversation links.
emails.felt_need: A link to an entire call recording is not a usable unit of feedback downstream; practitioners want the specific moment or comment isolated and routed, not the whole call, and existing tooling lacks a way to auto-route by fine-grained tag/hashtag into separate channels.
emails.mechanism: Autopilot reads call transcripts, support tickets, and reviews, extracts feature requests, merges duplicates, and triages feedback.
emails.belief_shift: Before: customer-conversation feedback still has to reach product as manually selected links or highlights. After: Canny offers a documented mechanism for extracting, deduplicating, and triaging that feedback automatically.
must_not_say: Ranking or weighting requests by account revenue/ARR on this free path.
Replacing or removing the incumbent Gong-to-ProductBoard and hashtag routing setup.
Any time saved or hours recovered; Hive's 2–3 hours per week is one customer's self-reported product-marketing result, not a promise.
Zero disruption, no setup effort, or no added headcount.
Routing feedback into separate hashtag-based Slack channels or topic buckets.
MCP server access, which requires a paid plan.
The $10K-versus-$500K example as proof of a Free or Autopilot ranking mechanism.
That every product team has this problem or uses Gong, Intercom, Slack, or ProductBoard.
That Autopilot guarantees correct extraction, prioritization, revenue growth, or roadmap outcomes.
Security, SSO, project-management integrations, Portal features, plan prices, and customer testimonials; they are separate arguments and would dilute this email.
Any claim that Canny is uniquely capable of this workflow or that competitors cannot perform it.
emails.objection: Will the product team still have to open every full conversation and clean up repeated requests manually?
emails.tone: Plain, confident, and product-focused, with short declarative sentences.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether Autopilot's documented capture, deduplication, and triage workflow is relevant enough to begin a free evaluation.
emails.next_step_value: The official page documents this verified fact: Autopilot automatically captures, deduplicates, and triages feedback, and is included in all plans.
emails.next_step_limit: The page does not establish setup effort, fit with the recipient's current stack, fine-grained hashtag routing into Slack channels, or ARR-based prioritization on the free path.
emails.subject_strategy: Lead with the concrete transformation from calls or tickets into usable feature requests. Avoid generic AI, feedback-management, productivity, and time-saving language.
